title: Centrifugal pump
object: ISO 2858 end-suction water pump 50-32-160 with its discharge globe valve, cut through the shaft and through the volute
idea: Converting rotation into pressure, and the operating point where supply meets demand
summary: The impeller flings water outwards and the volute turns its speed into pressure, so the stipple thickens from the suction eye to the discharge. The affinity laws scale the pump curve with speed, the globe valve steepens the system curve as it throttles, and the duty point sits where the two cross; below 1674 rpm the pump cannot lift the 12 m static head and nothing flows.
usedFor: Process-industry and maintenance training: reading a pump curve, throttling against speed control
Product documentation for pump and valve makers
Explaining an equilibrium point, supply meeting demand, as a software or economics metaphor
